rot.ideia.ex1.e1: There is a move in which two pieces move together: castling, with the king and the rook.
rot.ideia.ex1.e2: The king moves two squares towards the rook, to g1. The rook jumps over him and lands on f1.
rot.ideia.ex1.e3: To castle, you only move the king, two squares. The rook follows by itself.
rot.ideia.ex1.certo: That's right! The king went to g1 and the rook to f1. This is short castling.
rot.ideia.ex1.revela: The king goes to g1, and the rook jumps to f1.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.e1f1.1: The king moved only one square: that is not castling, and now he has lost the right to castle.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.e1f1.2: Let's go back: it is two squares.
rot.ideia.ex1.fora: That move is not castling. Let's go back: the king moves two squares towards the rook.
rot.ideia.ex1.l1: By castling, the king leaves the centre and is sheltered behind the pawns, and the rook joins the game.
rot.ideia.ex1.l2: Remember the idea: in castling, the king moves two squares and the rook jumps over him.
rot.ideia.ex2.e1: Now the rook is on the other side, on a1. You can also castle that way.
rot.ideia.ex2.e2: The squares between them, b1, c1 and d1, are empty. The king goes to c1, and the rook jumps to d1.
rot.ideia.ex2.p: Castle towards the rook on a1, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.certo: That's right! The king on c1 and the rook on d1: long castling.
rot.ideia.ex2.revela: The king goes to c1, and the rook jumps to d1.
rot.ideia.ex2.fora: That move is not castling. Let's go back: the king moves two squares towards the rook.
rot.ideia.ex2.volta: Castle towards the rook on a1, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.l1: This is long castling: the rook moves three squares. On the h1 side it moves only two: short castling.
rot.ideia.ex2.l2: Castling has rules. Now I will show when it cannot be done.
rot.demos.jaAndou.e1: First rule: the king and the rook must not have moved before.
rot.demos.jaAndou.l1: If the king takes a step...
rot.demos.jaAndou.l2: ...even if he comes back later, he has lost castling on both sides.
rot.demos.jaAndou.l3: If only one rook has moved, castling on that side is gone; the other side still counts.
rot.demos.casaAtacada.e1: Second rule: the king may not be in check, nor pass through an attacked square, nor end on one.
rot.demos.casaAtacada.e2: An attacked square is a square some black piece reaches.
rot.demos.casaAtacada.l1: Here the black bishop on a6 reaches f1, the square the king would pass through.
rot.demos.casaAtacada.l2: That is why short castling is forbidden in this position.
rot.demos.caminho.e1: Third rule: all the squares between the king and the rook must be empty.
rot.demos.caminho.l1: With the knight on b1 it is impossible. He moves out...
rot.demos.caminho.l2: ...and now long castling can be done.
rot.demos.caminho.l3: Now it's your turn: in the next positions, see which way castling is possible.
rot.pratica.umLado.enunciado: Castle, in one move. Look at the squares the king passes: one side is forbidden.
rot.pratica.umLado.fim: Perfect. The bishop was watching f1, so only long castling was possible.
rot.pratica.umLado.err.e1d1: The king moved only one square and lost the right to castle. Try again.
rot.pratica.umLado.err.e1d2: The king moved only one square and lost the right to castle. Try again.
rot.pratica.umLado.err.e1f2: The king moved only one square and lost the right to castle. Try again.
rot.pratica.ladoLivre.enunciado: Castle, in one move, towards the side where the way is clear.
rot.pratica.ladoLivre.fim: Well done. You now know how to castle and when it is allowed.
